answer: Clone wallets fail a one-booth sky plate they cannot share. An applicant posts 3.85 POA and books a 6-minute booth in a 21-bay planetarium. They press a 3.1 g sparrow-feather stylus into a wet plate, then spray an umber nebula of 44 calibrated droplets whose 17-byte landing hash is bound to their pubkey and the epoch seed, all within 48 seconds. 132 clones would pin 508.2 POA and need 132 exclusive booths. Graders replay the booth draw from the seed, count droplets to 1, and recompute the hash. A reused booth, droplet shortfall, or hash clash slashes 52% and closes that bay for 4 epochs.
